From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>

Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>

Subject: Quick recap + next steps (FinPay discovery)

Thanks again for taking the call earlier, Sarah — great to meet you and hear more about FinPay's roadmap for in-product conversational assistants. Quick recap and proposed next steps: 

Summary from our side
- Primary goal: reduce latency and inference cost for high-throughput payment assistant (peak 120 qps, expected 2M generation tokens/day).
- SLO: 95th percentile latency < 180ms for short responses (~64 tokens).
- Security: VPC/private deployment preferred, SOC2 + audit logs required.

What we discussed as priorities
1) Cost/unit economics comparison vs your current hyperscaler endpoints.
2) Real-world pilot with your workload to measure per-1M token cost, batching benefits, and cache hit improvement.
3) Procurement path and contract length for Dedicated capacity.

Proposed next steps
- We’ll send a concise TCO comparison (per-1M tokens) with assumptions and a short test plan — action: Marcus to own the numbers and write-up (cc'd).
- If that looks good, run a 72-hour pilot on a piece of production traffic (redacted) to measure latency, throughput, and cache hit rate.
- Procurement: Rachel will follow up on the security checklist and procurement lead.

Attachments: I’m attaching a one-page TCO spreadsheet and the FinPay requirements PDF you sent.

Open questions for your team
- Do you have a preferred sample traffic window (time of day / business days) for the pilot?
- Any non-standard security controls (HSM/KMS) we should include now?

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
aditya@redwood.com | (415) 555-0124

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@finpay.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Jun 2026 13:46:00 -0700
Subject: Redwood — concise TCO & unit economics (per your ask)

Hi Sarah / team — following up with the requested numbers. Attached a concise spreadsheet but summarizing the assumptions and results below so you can forward to your VP quickly.

Assumptions (baseline)
- Workload: prompt 40 tokens avg, response 80 tokens avg => 120 tokens per request.
- Volume: 2M gen tokens/day (production target) used to normalize to 1M tokens for unit costs.
- Latency SLO target: p95 < 180ms (short responses).
- Batching: conservative (2–4 concurrent requests per batch) vs best-case (10–20).
- Cache hit: conservative 15% prefix cache, realistic 30% after warm-up for repeated prompts (FAQ-style).
- Pricing photos: includes model runtime + infra + request overhead.

Per-1M tokens — generation (effective cost after batching & cache)
- Redwood (dedicated + optimized runtime):
  - Conservative case (low batching 2–4, cache hit 15%): $9.20 per 1M tokens
  - Realistic case (batching 6–10, cache hit 30%): $5.70 per 1M tokens
  - Best-case (high batching, high cache 50%): $3.80 per 1M tokens

- Hyperscaler A (managed endpoint; baseline single-request):
  - Conservative: $24.00 per 1M tokens
  - Realistic (their batching/autoscaling gains): $18.50 per 1M tokens

- Hyperscaler B (spot / flexible infra, higher variance): $15.00 per 1M tokens realistic

Notes on differences
- Batching gains: Redwood's runtime has continuous batching + optimized kernels — at real-world loads we see 2–4x token throughput improvement vs naive single-request endpoints. That directly reduces per-token GPU time.
- Cache: automatic prefix/KV caching reduces repeat work for FAQ/templated prompts — a 30% hit-rate reduces effective tokens served by ~30%.
- Tail latency: Redwood's routing and smaller-model fallbacks maintain p95 latency under load; hyperscalers often trade latency for cost with autoscaling steps.

Sample 1M-token calculation (realistic case)
- Raw 1M tokens -> after 30% cache hit => 700k tokens to serve.
- Effective GPU-time (batching reduces per-token time by ~40%) -> cost basis lowers further. Net cost: $5.70 / 1M tokens (see spreadsheet for line items).

Recommended next tests (to prove numbers on FinPay traffic)
1) 72-hour pilot on a representative subset (1k qps spike window) during morning peak. Measure: p50/p95 latency, observed batching factor, cache hit rate, total tokens served.
2) A/B test vs Hyperscaler endpoint for 24 hours (same traffic slice) to compare real costs and quality.
3) Run a synthetic stress-run to validate p95 at target throughput and measure fallbacks.

Deliverables from Redwood
- Short spreadsheet with per-token line items (attached).
- Pilot config + test plan (we'll provide infra handshake + limited access).

If this looks good we can lock the pilot start for Wednesday morning (June 30) during 9:00–12:00 PT.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com

- A 24-hour A/B comparison vs our current hyperscaler endpoint during the same pilot window (split traffic 50/50).
- Security handshake: we need KMS integration details and SOC2 evidence ahead of pilot; Rachel, can you share the checklist?

If you can send the pilot config and the DocuSign link for the pilot agreement today, we can route for an expedited signature.

—Sarah
